uncited: This family encompasses the numerical methods used to discretize and solve the Navier-Stokes equations for incompressible flow, producing the velocity and pressure fields that drive fluid simulation.
It solves the problem of computing physically plausible fluid motion (velocity, pressure, density) from a continuous partial differential equation into a discrete grid-based representation.

It is distinguished from particle-based methods (like [Position Based Fluids](1765-position-based-fluids.md)) by its Eulerian grid-based approach, and from pure advection methods (like [Smoke Advection](4639-smoke-advection.md)) by its inclusion of pressure projection and diffusion steps required to maintain incompressibility and viscosity.
All methods in this family solve the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on a staggered or collocated grid.

where $P$ is pressure, $m$ is molar mass, $g$ is gravity, $R$ is the universal gas constant, $T_0$ is ambient temperature, $T$ is advected temperature, and $\mathbf{z}$ is the normalized upward vector.
It represents a volume of gas as a combination of a scalar temperature field, a scalar pressure field, and a vector velocity field.
Smaller viscosity leads to more rotation.
These methods are widely used in visual effects for film and real-time rendering in games.
